Which integral  expression gives the arc length of the curve $h(t)=(2 \cos{\left(2 t \right)})\,i+(2 \sin{\left(2 t \right)})\,j+(3 t)\,k$ from $t=0$ to $t=2 \pi?$" :question/worked-solution "First, we find $h'(t)$ and $\|h'(t)\|:$

$$
\begin{aligned}h'(t) & =(\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(2 \cos{\left(2 t \right)}))\,i+(\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(2 \sin{\left(2 t \right)}))\,j+(\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(3 t))\,k \\  & =(- 4 \sin{\left(2 t \right)})\,i+(4 \cos{\left(2 t \right)})\,j+(3)\,k \\ \|h'(t)\| & =\sqrt{\left(- 4 \sin{\left(2 t \right)}\right)^{2} + \left(4 \cos{\left(2 t \right)}\right)^{2} + 3^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{16 \sin^{2}{\left(2 t \right)} + 16 \cos^{2}{\left(2 t \right)} + 9} \\  & =\sqrt{25}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the arc length of the curve is:

$$
\begin{aligned}L & =\int_{0}^{2 \pi}\|h'(t)\|\,\mathrm{d}t=\int_{0}^{2 \pi}\sqrt{25}\,\mathrm{d}t\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :question/answer-fields ["9bb4ed09-e6a2-579b-b4db-4bd11d2de44a"] :db/ensure :question/validate} {:db/id "5d4e5997-3f41-5fd4-846a-b8332280ee36" :answer/id #uuid "5d4e5997-3f41-5fd4-846a-b8332280ee36" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\int_{-1}^{1}\sqrt{\left(2 \sin{\left(2 t \right)} - $$

from  $t=0$ to $t=\pi?$" :question/worked-solution "First, we find $g'(t)$ and $\|g'(t)\|:$

$$
\begin{aligned}g'(t) & =\langle \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(4 t \sin{\left(t \right)}),\,\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(- 4 t \cos{\left(t \right)} - 2)\rangle \\  & =\langle 4 t \cos{\left(t \right)} + 4 \sin{\left(t \right)},\,4 t \sin{\left(t \right)} - 4 \cos{\left(t \right)}\rangle \\ \|g'(t)\| & =\sqrt{\left(4 t \sin{\left(t \right)} - 4 \cos{\left(t \right)}\right)^{2} + \left(4 t \cos{\left(t \right)} + 4 \sin{\left(t \right)}\right)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\left(16 t^{2} \sin^{2}{\left(t \right)} - 32 t \sin{\left(t \right)} \cos{\left(t \right)} + 16 \cos^{2}{\left(t \right)}\right) + \left(16 t^{2} \cos^{2}{\left(t \right)} + 32 t \sin{\left(t \right)} \cos{\left(t \right)} + 16 \sin^{2}{\left(t \right)}\right)} \\  & =\sqrt{16 t^{2} + 16}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the arc length of the curve is:

$$
\begin{aligned}L & =\int_{0}^{\pi}\|g'(t)\|\,\mathrm{d}t=\int_{0}^{\pi}4 \sqrt{t^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}t\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["c148f967-914b-5a44-9dde-6d1d5884252f"] :db/ensure :question/validate} {:db/id "e9ba3779-d05c-5cec-81d9-ad998ebc62b6" :answer/id #uuid "e9ba3779-d05c-5cec-81d9-ad998ebc62b6" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\int_{-1}^{1}\sqrt{\left(\sin{\left(3 t \right)} -
